market_name: Will 10 Fed rate cuts happen in 2026?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether 2y/10y Treasury yields are actually falling and if fed funds futures (SOFR/SR3) are repricing dovishly; confirm the prediction-market move isn't isolated noise.
time_plan.1h: Cross-check TLT price vs the move in front-end rate futures; look for any breaking macro headline (jobs, financial-stability event) that would justify emergency-cut pricing.
time_plan.2h: Reassess whether the dovish repricing is broad (equities, gold, USD all confirming) or a one-off in the extreme strike.
time_plan.6h: Evaluate whether TLT sustained direction; fade if move reverses toward baseline with no supporting data.
time_plan.12h: Mark final TLT return vs entry; log whether the tail-strike probability move had any predictive value for rates.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of 10 Fed cuts in 2026 (250bps of easing) is an extreme dovish/recession signal. Aggressive expected easing pulls the entire yield curve lower, which lifts long-duration Treasury prices. TLT is the most liquid, high-beta expression of falling long-end yields. However, 10 cuts is a deep tail scenario, so a probability move here likely reflects thin, speculative positioning rather than fresh macro information.

predictions.tradable_instrument_name: Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check DXY and EUR/USD, JPY moves alongside front-end US rates to see if the rate-differential story or the safe-haven story dominates.
time_plan.1h: Confirm whether USD weakness aligns with falling US real yields; watch for risk-off flows that could flip the sign.
time_plan.2h: Reassess dollar direction against equity/VIX behavior — risk-off would undermine the thesis.
time_plan.6h: Determine if UUP move persisted; abandon thesis if dollar strengthens on haven demand.
time_plan.12h: Record final UUP return and note whether the dovish signal or haven flows dominated.

predictions.reasoning: Pricing in ten 25bp cuts implies a collapse in US short-term rate expectations relative to other economies, which typically weakens the dollar via narrowing rate differentials. UUP would drift lower. But the linkage is weak in a 12h window: a global recession scare can paradoxically strengthen the dollar as a safe haven, muddying the sign, hence low confidence and a wide, sign-straddling interval.

evidence_used: Market question implies 250bps of Fed easing in 2026, an extreme dovish/recession tail scenario
Standard macro transmission: aggressive expected cuts lower yields (bonds up) and narrow rate differentials (USD down)
700bps tradability threshold is extreme for broad liquid ETFs over 12h
Deep out-of-strike prediction markets tend to be thin and speculative

Recession fears can strengthen the dollar (safe haven), inverting the FX call
Neither proxy is likely to move 700bps in 12h, so neither is 'tradable' by the stated threshold

llm_justification.summary: This market prices an extreme scenario of ten Fed rate cuts (250bps) in 2026. A sharp rise in that probability would signal deep recession/emergency-easing expectations, implying lower yields (long Treasuries/TLT up) and, less reliably, a softer dollar (UUP down). Both mappings are macro-sensible but weak in a 12h window: the strike is a thin tail, safe-haven flows can flip the FX sign, and neither liquid proxy plausibly moves the 700bps needed to be tradable. Treat as low-confidence research signals, not actionable trades.
key_assumptions: A probability move reflects genuine macro repricing rather than illiquid speculation
Rate-cut expectations transmit conventionally to bond prices and FX
No offsetting shock (e.g., inflation surprise) dominates the window
failure_modes: The tail-strike move is noise/liquidity-driven and reverses within hours
Recession scare triggers safe-haven USD buying, inverting the FX prediction
The dovish scenario was already public/priced into rates, leaving no leakage edge
Broad ETF proxies are too low-beta to reach the 700bps tradable threshold, making signals immaterial
Bond selloff on fiscal/inflation concerns could push TLT down despite cut expectations
